applicability: The last block of a dimension does not divide evenly into the tile.
A dynamic batch or sequence length is smaller than the fixed tile.
A softmax or max reduction must ignore padded tail elements.
directions: Use `pl.load(x, [row, 0], [TILE, COLS], valid_shape=[valid_rows, COLS])` for a dynamic row count.
Use `pl.slice(x, [TILE, COLS], [offset, 0], valid_shape=[valid_rows, COLS], pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)` when the tail must mask a max reduction.
After an on-chip computation with a runtime extent, use `pl.set_validshape(t, rows, cols)`; do not apply it to a slice/reshape view.
Use `pl.fillpad(scores, pad_value=pl.PadValue.min)` before a softmax `row_max`; use `pl.tile.fillpad_inplace` only when buffer sharing is intended.
Use `pl.reshape` for a zero-copy layout change and verify that the source valid region maps to an origin-anchored box of the new shape.
effects: A fixed tile with a smaller valid region keeps a stable allocation and layout but carries padding through reductions and stores.
`fillpad_inplace` saves a buffer but aliases the input, which interacts with memory reuse and later readers.
Dropping unit dimensions simplifies downstream shapes but is only legal when the dim is static, unit, and fully valid.
invariants: `pl.slice` argument order is `(input, shape, offset)`; `pl.load` is `(tensor, offsets, shapes)`; `pl.store` is `(tile, offsets, output_tensor)`.
A tile `pl.slice` has no `clamp`; `offset + shape` must stay inside the source. Tensor slicing does expose `clamp=True`.
Only `pl.PadValue.zero`, `pl.PadValue.max`, and `pl.PadValue.min` are hardware padding modes; arbitrary sentinels are rejected. `drop_dims` entries must be static unit dims that remain fully valid.
`pl.reshape` rejects a partial valid region that cannot be described by the target shape.
principle: `pl.slice(tensor, shape, offset, valid_shape=..., drop_dims=..., pad_value=..., clamp=...)` takes a sub-region with shape before offset. `pl.load(tensor, offsets, shapes, valid_shape=..., target_memory=..., clamp=..., cache=...)` uses the opposite order: offsets before shapes. `pl.store(tile, offsets, output_tensor, shapes=..., atomic=..., st_phase=...)` writes a tile back. `pl.assemble(target, source, offset, atomic=...)` writes a source into a target at an offset. A slice or load is never valid where the source is not: the source's valid region, shifted by the offset and cut to the window, bounds the result. `valid_shape` narrows; it cannot widen. A tensor slice with `clamp=True` sanctions a window that runs off the source and cuts the valid region to the source edge; a tile slice has no `clamp` because an on-chip window cannot overhang. `drop_dims` erases static unit axes from the result type; tile rank is clamped back to 2D. `pl.set_validshape(tile, valid_rows, valid_cols)` annotates an already-computed 2D tile when the valid extent is known only at runtime. It is not accepted on a view (a slice or reshape result), because that view already carries its valid extent; narrow at the slice with `valid_shape=` instead. `pl.fillpad(tile, pad_value=...)` rewrites only the invalid tail of a tile; the tile-only `pl.tile.fillpad_inplace` does it in place and shares the input buffer; `pl.fillpad_expand` copies a smaller source into a larger destination. The pad value matters for reductions: a max over a zero-padded partial tile returns at least zero, so use `pl.PadValue.min` for max and zero for sum. `pl.reshape` is a zero-copy view and never widens the valid region; a partial region that no origin-anchored box of the new shape can describe is rejected. `pl.reinterpret_view` changes dtype over the same bytes, and `pl.transpose` swaps axes.
questions: The exact set of partial-region reshapes that the installed compiler accepts is best established by compiling the concrete shape pair.
risks: Using `pl.PadValue.zero` for a max reduction over an all-negative row, silently returning zero.
Applying `set_validshape` to a slice or reshape result; the view already owns its valid extent.
Passing a float expression such as `n / 2` where an integer offset is required; offsets and shapes must be integer scalars.
Assuming a reshape can widen a partial valid region; it is carried through, never invented.
Calling a top-level `pl.fillpad_inplace`; only `pl.tile.fillpad_inplace` is exposed.
source_features: pl.slice(tensor, shape, offset, valid_shape=..., drop_dims=..., pad_value=..., clamp=...)
pl.load(tensor, offsets, shapes, valid_shape=..., target_memory=..., clamp=..., cache=...)
pl.store(tile, offsets, output_tensor, shapes=..., atomic=..., st_phase=...)
summary: A tile has an allocated shape and an optional valid region. Loads and slices only read source bytes that exist, reductions see the padding, and `fillpad`/`set_validshape` make the tail explicit. Argument order and view restrictions differ between `pl.slice`, `pl.load`, and `pl.store`.
title: Slicing, Valid Shapes, Padding, and Shape Views
